description: Teachers are asked to speak for education policy constantly and asked about their actual craft almost never. Invert that and the interview transforms.

questions.text: What can you tell about a class in the first week that shapes the whole year?
questions.lands_because: Classroom read is a real and highly developed skill, and asking about it treats teaching as expertise rather than as vocation.
followups: What do you do differently once you know?

questions.text: What is the difference between a lesson that works and the same lesson falling flat?
questions.lands_because: Same material, different outcome - it isolates the teaching itself from the curriculum, which is exactly the thing that is hard to name and rarely credited.
followups: Can you feel it going wrong in real time? What do you do?

questions.text: How much of your job is teaching, and what is the rest?
questions.lands_because: Opens onto documentation, meetings, behavior management, counseling, and family communication - the parts that expanded without anyone deciding they should.
followups: When did the rest start growing?

questions.text: What does a student learn from you that no test will ever pick up?
questions.lands_because: Lets a teacher speak about what they actually value, in direct contrast to the measurement regime they work under, without asking them to attack it.
followups: Does anyone in the building measure that?

questions.text: What reform arrived with a mandate and a training day and then quietly disappeared?
questions.lands_because: Teachers have watched a decade of these and are rarely asked to evaluate them. The answers are specific, funny, and often furious.
followups: Was any of it good? What should have survived?

questions.text: Which student do you still think about?
questions.lands_because: Almost always produces the emotional center of the episode. Place it late, ask it quietly, and do not fill the silence.
questions.avoid_if: Early in the interview, or with a guest who has stayed formal. It needs a warmed-up room.
